roles.text: First mate of the Pharaon, aged 19
Prisoner No. 34 at the Château d’If

notes.text: Brings the ship home after the captain dies at sea; Morrel means to make him captain. On the captain’s orders he stopped at Elba and came away with a letter for Paris.
Finds his father going hungry because of Caderousse’s demand.
Engaged to Mercédès.
Arrested at his betrothal feast.
Tells Villefort everything. Villefort burns the letter, makes him swear silence and has him held.
Taken to the Château d’If. Moved to a dungeon after threatening a jailer.
Begs a visiting inspector for a trial. The register calls him a dangerous Bonapartist.
Close to starving himself when he hears digging. Meets Faria.
Sees Faria’s cell and inventions.
Learns from Faria who betrayed him and why. Swears revenge and becomes Faria’s pupil.
Told of the Spada treasure on Monte Cristo.
Faria dies.
Takes Faria’s place in the burial sack and is thrown into the sea.
Elderly and poor, living alone. While Edmond was at sea, Caderousse pressed him to repay a debt of Edmond’s, and he went hungry on what was left.
Sees his son arrested at the feast.
Waits alone for news.
Dies, destitute and grieving. Morrel pays for the funeral.
Edmond is keen to see her after the voyage.
Lives in the Catalan village. Turns down her cousin Fernand because she loves Edmond.
Sees Edmond arrested.
Asks Villefort what has become of Edmond and gets no answer. Fernand stays close to her.
Left alone when Fernand is called up.
Head of the shipping firm Morrel & Son. Fair to his crew and fond of Edmond.
At the feast; goes to find out why Edmond was arrested.
Tells Villefort that Edmond is innocent.
While Napoleon is back in power, asks Villefort to free Edmond. Villefort drafts a petition that makes Edmond look a committed Bonapartist, and keeps it. Pays for Old Dantès’s funeral.
The ship’s business agent, in charge of cargo and accounts. Resents Edmond’s promotion and watched him go ashore at Elba. The final s is silent.
Writes the anonymous letter accusing Edmond, left-handed to disguise it, then throws it aside.
Leaves Marseille for Spain to work for a banker.
Faria identifies him as the letter’s author.
In love with Mercédès and bitter that she chose Edmond.
Danglars works on his jealousy. Picks up the discarded letter.
Stays close to Mercédès.
Called up to the army and leaves Marseille.
Faria works out that he sent the letter.
Envious and a heavy drinker. Made Old Dantès repay a debt of Edmond’s.
Present, and drunk, when the letter is written. Objects, but does nothing.
Suspects the letter is behind the arrest.
Also called up to the army.
Young, ambitious and loudly royalist. Called away from his own betrothal dinner to deal with Edmond.
Finds the letter is addressed to his own father. Burns it and has Edmond held to protect himself.
Sends Edmond to the Château d’If.
Leaves for Paris to be first to warn the king.
Warns Louis XVIII of the Bonapartist plot.
Wins the king’s favour when news of Napoleon’s landing arrives.
Warns his father the police have his description, then returns to Marseille.
Survives Napoleon’s return thanks to his father. Buries Morrel’s petition for Edmond.
Faria works out why he buried the case.
Uneasy at the table talk of trials and executions. Asks Villefort to be lenient with his prisoner.
Sees Villefort briefly before he leaves for Paris.
An old aristocrat loyal to the Bourbon king. Host of the betrothal dinner.
A fierce royalist. Raises the awkward fact that Villefort’s father backed the Revolution; Villefort insists on his own loyalty to the king.

roles.text: Villefort’s father, an active Bonapartist in Paris

notes.text: A former revolutionary. Villefort has dropped his father’s surname to keep clear of his politics.
The letter Edmond carried was addressed to him, rue Coq-Héron, Paris.
Calls on Villefort, hints he knows what happened to Quesnel, then escapes in disguise after Villefort warns him.
Protects his son while Napoleon is back in power.
The restored Bourbon king, to whom Villefort and the Saint-Mérans are loyal.
Makes light of warnings about Napoleon until Villefort arrives.
Hears Napoleon has landed. Rewards Villefort.
Loses the throne to Napoleon, then regains it after Waterloo.
Brings Villefort’s warning to the king.
Humiliated when Napoleon lands without his ministry knowing.
Thought mad because he keeps offering the governor a fortune for his freedom.
His escape tunnel comes out in Edmond’s cell by mistake.
Shows Edmond the tools, pens, ink and lamp he has made, and the book he wrote on linen.
Works out who betrayed Edmond and why. Teaches him languages, science and history.
Partly paralysed after a seizure. Reveals the Spada treasure and where it lies.
Dies after a third seizure.
Died of brain fever on the voyage. His last order sent Edmond to Elba with a package.
The man Edmond handed the captain’s package to.
“The Emperor” to his supporters, “the usurper” to royalists. Edmond met him briefly on Elba.
Villefort reports a plot for his return.
Lands in France. Royalists call him “the Corsican ogre”.
Retakes the throne for the Hundred Days, then is defeated at Waterloo.
Went to a Bonapartist meeting in the rue Saint-Jacques and was later found dead. The police want a man seen with him.
Noirtier hints he knows what happened.

roles.text: A wealthy cardinal in Renaissance Rome

notes.text: Poisoned by the Borgias in 1498. Hid his fortune before he died.
He and his father poisoned rich cardinals to take their money. Cardinal Spada was one.
Faria was his secretary. Among his family papers Faria found the clue to the treasure.
